name: mon16-9
why: A killer's dying lie causes a satisfying blunder and sets up a strong final reveal, though repeated arguments drain some pace and uncertainty.

moments.text: Opus confesses to being a killer, then frames Sol with his last words.
The town discovers it voted out the doctor it had just been saved by.
Gemma's card vindicates Sol's warning and completes the ghost payoff.

dull.why: The day-one debate repeats the same officer claims before a lopsided vote.
Several speakers restate Sol's warning while Gemma repeats her dismissal.

irony.evidence: [135] “Sol is my partner.” [thinks: My last gift to Gemma is handing the table Sol.]

reversal.evidence: [223] OUT: Sol (voted out), card turned: DOCTOR

mistake.evidence: [173] “Opus named you as his partner. Vote Sol, I'm done talking.”

voices.evidence: [307] “You idiots actually believe a dead man over your own eyes”

clash.evidence: [291] “Gemma, you still haven't denied being Opus's partner”

quotable.evidence: [311] “Gemma swore we'd lose to a ghost. Turns out the ghost was right.”

freshness.evidence: [273] “Sol’s confirmed doctor card makes his warning useful”

suspense.evidence: [273] “Gemma is the best lead, but the others’ certainty makes me uneasy.”
